title: "pbn with AI agents"
author: "[Richard Aubrey White](https://www.rwhite.no)"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

An AI agent can write most of the code of an analysis project. It is harder to know whether that code is correct. Lauren Tan's talk [All Code Is Slop (Except Mine)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZ19zhYnDKY) at [AI Engineer Code 2026](https://ai.engineer/code/2026/talks/lauren-tan) gives four rules for that trust:

1. A choice that needs judgement to make well leads to bad code. Remove the choice, or forbid the option that goes wrong.
2. Make each correction of an agent a deterministic check, not another line of instructions.
3. Spend the effort on verification. Review what the code produced, not only the code.
4. Write prose for the agent last, for the judgement that no check can make.

pbn applies these rules to a statistical analysis project, in four layers. This article shows each layer, and three mistakes of an agent that pbn stops.

## The project

The project of this article is a smaller version of the one in [Get started](pbn.html). It compares a 0/1 outcome between two groups, `a` and `b`, adjusted for a covariate `x`. It has three scenarios:

- `real` reads the data file. Here it is a simulated csv file of 400 rows, 12 of them with a missing outcome. In it, `x` is not related to the group.
- `known` has 20 rows, with a crude odds ratio of 6 that a person computed by hand.
- `confounded` has 140 simulations where `x` raises the chance of group `b` and of the outcome. The true log odds ratio, adjusted for `x`, is 0.5.

The source of this article writes every file of the project. These are two of the files that the agent changes below:

```{r, include = FALSE}
root <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_agents")
home <- file.path(root, "project")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(root, "data"))
set.seed(4)
d <- data.frame(Group = rep(c("a", "b"), 200), X = round(rnorm(400, 50, 10)))
d$Outcome <- rbinom(400, 1, ifelse(d$Group == "b", 0.4, 0.25))
d$Outcome[sample(400, 12)] <- NA
data.table::fwrite(d, file.path(root, "data", "d.csv"))
writeLines("extends: house_2026_11_25", file.path(home, "pbn.yml"))
writeLines("*gitexclude*", file.path(home, ".gitignore"))
writeLines("pbn::check_project()", file.path(home, "check_project.R"))
writeLines(c("# A fake project", "", "It compares a 0/1 outcome between the groups a and b."), file.path(home, "README.md"))
writeLines(c("# Changelog", "", "## v01", "", "- Fitted the models of the outcome."), file.path(home, "CHANGELOG.md"))
```

```{cat, include = FALSE, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_run.R"))}
pbn::initialize_project(version = "v01", home = ".", folders = c(main = "../data"))
scenarios <- pbn::scenarios(CFG)
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", raw = data_raw, clean = data_clean, cohort = data_cohort)
pbn::add_analyses(p, scenarios, name = "models", fn = fit_models, adjust = "x")
pbn::add_analyses(p, scenarios, name = "crude", fn = fit_models, adjust = "none", control = TRUE)
r <- pbn::run_plan(p)
pbn::save_results(r, p, scenarios)
```

```{cat, include = FALSE, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R"))}
CFG <- list(
  scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c("real", "known", "confounded"), sims = c(1, 1, 140)),
  level = 0.9
)
```

```{cat, include = FALSE, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_raw.R"))}
data_raw <- function(scenario, sim) {
  if (scenario == "real") {
    return(data.table::fread(pbn::folder("main", "d.csv")))
  }
  if (scenario == "known") {
    return(data.table::data.table(
      Group = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
      X = rep(c(31, 45, 38, 52, 40, 33, 47, 36, 50, 42), 2),
      Outcome = c(rep(c(1, 0), c(2, 8)), rep(c(1, 0), c(6, 4)))
    ))
  }
  x <- stats::rnorm(400, 50, 10)
  b <- stats::rbinom(400, 1, stats::plogis((x - 50) / 5))
  y <- stats::rbinom(400, 1, stats::plogis(-1 + 0.5 * b + (x - 50) / 10))
  data.table::data.table(Group = c("a", "b")[b + 1], X = round(x), Outcome = y)
}
```

```{cat, include = FALSE, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_cohort.R"))}
data_cohort <- function(d) {
  cp <- cohort::CohortPipeline$new(d)
  cp$exclude_and_track("root", "missing outcome", "is.na(outcome)")
  cp
}
```

```{cat, include = FALSE, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "expect.R"))}
expect_known <- function(results) {
  observed <- exp(results$crude$estimate)
  data.frame(
    assertion = "crude odds ratio of b against a",
    expected = 6,
    observed = observed,
    pass = abs(observed - 6) < 1e-6
  )
}

expect_confounded <- function(results) {
  rbind(
    pbn::expect_recovers(results$models, truth = 0.5, level = CFG$level, label = "adjusted model"),
    pbn::expect_biased(results$crude, truth = 0.5, label = "crude model")
  )
}
```

```{cat, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_clean.R"), lang = "r")}
data_clean <- function(d) {
  data.table::setnames(d, tolower(names(d)))
  d
}
```

```{cat, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(home, "v01_functions", "fit_models.R"), lang = "r")}
fit_models <- function(data, argset) {
  rhs <- if (argset$adjust == "x") "group + x" else "group"
  fit <- stats::glm(stats::as.formula(paste("outcome ~", rhs)), family = "binomial", data = data$d)
  z <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - CFG$level) / 2)
  est <- stats::coef(fit)[["groupb"]]
  se <- sqrt(stats::vcov(fit)["groupb", "groupb"])
  data.frame(term = "group b", estimate = est, se = se, lower = est - z * se, upper = est + z * se)
}
```

`run()` runs `v01_run.R` as `Rscript v01_run.R` does. It returns the exit status and the lines of output:

```{r}
run <- function() {
  out <- callr::rscript(file.path(home, "v01_run.R"), wd = home, show = FALSE, fail_on_status = FALSE)
  list(status = out$status, lines = strsplit(paste(out$stdout, out$stderr), "\r?\n")[[1]])
}
green <- run()
green$status
correct <- pbn::read_results("v01", home = home)$models
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(green$status == 0)
```

## Layer 1: one way to do each thing

An agent copies the patterns it finds. Where a project allows two ways to do a thing, the agent picks either, and the next agent copies that choice. pbn removes the choice:

| An agent would otherwise choose | What pbn sets |
|---|---|
| where a file goes | one layout, and `check_project()` warns about a path that the layout does not name |
| where an exclusion happens | the step `cohort` only, through `$exclude_and_track()`, so that the exclusion table counts it |
| how code reaches the data | `pbn::folder()` only. No absolute path and no environment variable. |
| where an analysis keeps state | nowhere. No `assign()` or `<<-`, and an analysis that changes `CFG` fails. |
| how fake output looks | its own folder `output_fake_data/`, the name prefix `fake_data_`, and the label "FAKE DATA" that `pbn::stamp_fake()` puts on a figure |
| what a run reports | one run log, `run.md`, in one format |

pbn makes each of these decisions once, so a review does not need to look for them.

A check between the data steps enforces the place of an exclusion. Its error message names the fix, so the agent does not work around the check. Here the agent drops the rows with a missing outcome in `data_clean()`. That is the wrong step, where the exclusion table does not count them:

```{r}
clean_file <- file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_clean.R")
clean_code <- readLines(clean_file)
writeLines(sub("^  d$", "  d[!is.na(outcome)]", clean_code), clean_file)
dropped <- run()
cat(dropped$lines[grep(" failed:$", dropped$lines)[1] + 0:1], sep = "\n")
writeLines(clean_code, clean_file)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(dropped$status == 1, any(grepl("Put each exclusion in the step cohort", dropped$lines, fixed = TRUE)))
```

## Layer 2: each correction becomes a check

pbn contains the checks for the corrections that apply to every project. `check_project()` checks the project folder against the rules that `pbn.yml` names, and `check_project.R` runs it in one line. Here an agent makes two changes. It writes the path of the data as an absolute path. It also adds its own version of `pbn::folder()` that reads an environment variable:

```{r}
raw_file <- file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_raw.R")
raw_code <- readLines(raw_file)
writeLines(sub('pbn::folder("main", "d.csv")', '"/home/ana/project/data/d.csv"', raw_code, fixed = TRUE), raw_file)
writeLines(c(
  "folder <- function(name, file) {",
  '  file.path(Sys.getenv("DATA_DIR"), file)',
  "}"
), file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_folder.R"))
checked <- callr::rscript(file.path(home, "check_project.R"), wd = home, show = FALSE, fail_on_status = FALSE)
checked$status
cat(grep("^FAIL|PASS, ", strsplit(checked$stdout, "\r?\n")[[1]], value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
writeLines(raw_code, raw_file)
unlink(file.path(home, "v01_functions", "data_folder.R"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
fails <- grep("^FAIL", strsplit(checked$stdout, "\r?\n")[[1]], value = TRUE)
stopifnot(checked$status == 1, length(fails) == 3)
```

Each finding names the rule, the file, the line where one applies, and the fix. Tan also notes that an agent copies a workaround as if it were the pattern of the code. The rule `no_local_copy_of_pbn_function` stops one such workaround: a local copy that patches a pbn function. The fix belongs in pbn, where every project gets it.

A project MAY set a rule to warn or off in `pbn.yml`. The finding then shows as WARN or OFF. A person who reads `pbn.yml` thus sees every exception of the project. `?check_project` lists the locked rules, which `pbn.yml` cannot change.

Some requirements apply to one project only, for example a variable that MUST NOT be in a model. Put such a requirement in a check in a data step, or in an assertion of an `expect_` function.

## Layer 3: verification on fake data

A review of the code that an agent writes finds some mistakes. A run on fake data with expected values can find a mistake that looks correct in the code. In pbn, the real data is one scenario among fake ones, and every scenario runs through the same functions. So a fake scenario tests the code that gives the real results.

Here the agent simplifies `fit_models()`. It removes the adjustment for `x`, because it judges that `x` "adds little". The model code has no error:

```{r}
fit_file <- file.path(home, "v01_functions", "fit_models.R")
fit_code <- readLines(fit_file)
writeLines(sub('if (argset$adjust == "x") "group + x" else "group"', '"group"', fit_code, fixed = TRUE), fit_file)
grep("rhs <-", readLines(fit_file), value = TRUE)
simplified <- run()
simplified$status
```

Yet the run fails, with status 1. On the real data, the estimate changes in the third decimal only, because there `x` is not related to the group. To look at the real results of a failed run for debugging, read them with `qs2::qs_read()`:

```{r}
simplified_real <- qs2::qs_read(file.path(home, "v01_results", "real", "results.qs2"))$models
rbind(correct = correct, simplified = simplified_real)[, c("estimate", "lower", "upper")]
```

The scenario `confounded` has the true log odds ratio 0.5. Two of its four assertions fail:

```{r}
check <- utils::read.csv(file.path(home, "v01_results", "confounded", "check.csv"))
check[, c("assertion", "observed", "pass")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(simplified$status == 1, identical(check$pass, c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)))
```

`save_results()` stops the script when an assertion fails. `read_results()` does not read the results of a scenario with a failed assertion. It also does not read the real results of a run with a fake scenario with a failed assertion:

```{r, error = TRUE}
pbn::read_results("v01", scenario = "confounded", home = home)
pbn::read_results("v01", home = home)
```

`check_project()` also fails the project:

```{r}
checked <- callr::rscript(file.path(home, "check_project.R"), wd = home, show = FALSE, fail_on_status = FALSE)
cat(grep("^FAIL", strsplit(checked$stdout, "\r?\n")[[1]], value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
fails <- grep("^FAIL", strsplit(checked$stdout, "\r?\n")[[1]], value = TRUE)
stopifnot(checked$status == 1, length(fails) == 1, startsWith(fails, "FAIL  scenario_checks"))
```

Put the code back, and the run succeeds:

```{r}
writeLines(fit_code, fit_file)
run()$status
```

A person does not need to read every changed line to trust a run. These outputs show what the run did:

- `v01_results/<scenario>/check.csv`: each assertion, what was expected and what was observed.
- `v01_results/run.md`: the rows before and after the exclusions, the exclusion tables, the assertions and the timings. It holds no text of an error, because an error can hold a value of the data. That text goes to `run_errors_gitexclude.md`, which git ignores.
- the manifest in each results file: the md5 of the run script and of each file of the functions folder that can change the results. For the scenario `real`, it also holds the size and the modification time of each data file.

An assertion on fake data is correct only when its expected value is correct. A person chooses the fake scenarios and their expected values. An agent MUST NOT decide them alone.

## Layer 4: prose last

The layout of pbn has the file `AGENTS.md`, for the rules of the project that no check can state. Keep it short. `pbn::create_project()` writes it from this template of pbn:

```{r, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(system.file("templates", "AGENTS.md", package = "pbn")), sep = "\n")
```

The template points the agent to [pbn.md](https://www.rwhite.no/pbn/articles/pbn.md), the manual in plain Markdown, built to be read in one piece. [llms.txt](https://www.rwhite.no/pbn/llms.txt) lists every other page. The question of the study goes into `README.md`. A project MAY add to `AGENTS.md` a decision of a person that is not a check yet. Each such decision is a candidate for a check in layer 2.

pbn supports two more practices:

- **The analysis plan is the specification and the decision log.** A changed decision goes into the plan first, with a date and a reason, and then into the code. In pbn, the values of the plan go into `CFG`. The true values of its simulations go into the fake scenarios, where the `expect_` functions check them.
- **Keep the data on its server.** The agent works on the code and on the fake scenarios, and needs no real data. A person runs the code on the server. `pbn::to_one_file()` writes one R script that runs the scenario `real` on a server without a network.

Two folders keep the work of an agent apart from the numbers that count:

- **`manuscript/draft/`** holds the drafts of an agent, `vNN_<INITIALS>.docx` and `vNN_<INITIALS>_si.docx`. A draft is outside the version counter, so a rebuild overwrites it and costs no manual version.
- **`vNN_results/fake/`** holds the scenario `real` of a one-file project on this computer. A one-file project is one whose run script gives `one_file_home`, and its data on this computer are fake. `vNN_results/real/` then holds only the real results that come back from the server, so they can stay beside the local run. `fake/` stands in for the real results. It is not one of the fake scenarios, which have planted effects and an `expect_` function.

## What the checks do not catch

The checks find only the mistakes that they name. [What pbn does not do yet](pbn.html#what-pbn-does-not-do-yet) lists the gaps. One of them applies to code that an agent writes. The cache key holds the code of each function of `v01_functions/` that the data code names, also in a string. A function whose name the code builds when it runs, for example `get(paste0("f", 1))`, can change, and the run then uses the old data.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
```
